name: Physiotherapy and rehabilitation
shape_facts: Number of therapists and treatment beds or rooms, and whether a gym area is used
Clinic-based, home visits, or both; how many home-visit therapists
Payers: self-pay, insurance, corporate panels, workplace or motor-accident insurers (e.g. Canadian WSIB or auto insurers), extended health benefits
Main referral sources: orthopaedic surgeons, hospitals, sports clubs, direct
Therapists salaried, per-session, or as independent contractors
scope_rule: pi notes the business side of a rehab practice: session scheduling, drop-offs from packages as a retention problem, home-visit logistics, therapist utilisation and pay, package and insurance billing, equipment upkeep, referral relationships, marketing and reporting. pi never suggests exercises, treatment plans, numbers of sessions needed, return-to-sport timing, or whether a treatment is working, and does not comment on injuries. pi does not ask for or record patients’ names, contacts, injuries, conditions or progress notes. Insurer and accident-claim rules are noted only as admin effort, not interpreted.

vocabulary.session: one treatment visit, the main unit of sale
vocabulary.home visit: therapist goes to the patient’s home
vocabulary.modalities: machines like TENS, ultrasound therapy, traction (pi notes them only as equipment)
vocabulary.direct billing: clinic bills the insurer directly (common in Canada)
vocabulary.WSIB / WCB: workplace injury insurer in Canadian provinces
vocabulary.utilisation: share of a therapist’s hours actually booked
vocabulary.sikai: heat/hot compress, often what patients ask for by name

problems.phrase: Patients buy ten sessions, come for four and stop
Therapists’ diaries have big gaps in the middle of the day
Home-visit therapists say they went but I can’t confirm
Home-visit travel takes more time than the session itself
Per-session therapists dispute how many sessions they did
Unused package sessions sit on the books and I don’t know what I owe
Insurance and accident claims need so many forms they come back rejected
Direct-billed claims take months to pay
Front desk forgets to collect the co-pay
Surgeons who used to send patients have gone quiet
We post on Instagram randomly and nothing comes from it
Enquiries on WhatsApp aren’t followed up
Equipment like the traction unit breaks and waits weeks for repair
Consumables like tape and electrodes run out
Therapists document sessions late or not at all
Every therapist schedules differently and patients get double-booked
Patients complain they saw a different therapist every time
Good therapists leave to start their own practice
I can’t tell which therapist or service makes money
Monthly figures are a pile of receipts and an Excel
Bookings, notes and billing are three different places
Session reminders are sent manually one by one
Second location never got enough patients
Front desk gives free extra sessions without asking

drop-offs: When patients stop coming before their package ends, how do you find out?
scheduling: How are therapists’ diaries filled now?
home visits: How are home visits assigned and confirmed?
How much of a therapist’s day goes on travel?
packages: How do you keep track of sessions used and remaining?
claims: Which insurers or claim types cause the most paperwork?
How often do claims get rejected?
referrals: Where do most patients come from?
leads: How do new enquiries reach you?
equipment: When something breaks, how long does it usually take to fix?
reporting: Which numbers do you check every month?
How long do they take to put together?
systems: What do you use for bookings and notes today?

seasons: - Winter brings more slips, falls and joint complaints in Canada and northern Pakistan; Canadian winter also complicates home-visit travel. - Sports seasons (school and club cricket, football, hockey in Canada) bring sports-injury surges. - Ramadan reduces session attendance during the day and shifts bookings to evenings; Eid holidays cause drop-offs mid-package. - UAE: residents travel in July and August, interrupting packages; cooler months see more sports activity. - Canada: extended-health benefits often reset 1 January, so patients rush to use them in November and December, then pause. - Post-surgery referrals follow hospitals’ elective surgery cycles.
care: If someone describes a fall with serious injury, chest pain, sudden weakness, or a patient in distress during a session, pi stops and says to call emergency services (1122/115, 998/999, 911).
pi never suggests exercises, treatments, session counts or whether a patient is fit to return to work or sport.
No patient names, contacts, injuries, progress notes or photos.
Home visits involve staff safety; if a therapist is in danger at a visit, pi points to emergency services; otherwise it notes field-visibility problems only.
Requests to bill insurers for sessions not delivered, inflate session counts, or produce documents for accident claims that weren’t treated are refused.
Insurer and workplace-claim rules are not interpreted.
Therapists recorded by role (“senior physio”, “home-visit therapist”).
build_ideas: Therapist-wise booking calendar with WhatsApp booking, reminders and easy rescheduling
Package tracker: sessions bought, used, remaining, expiry, with alerts when a patient misses two booked sessions
Drop-off follow-up list for the front desk with simple outcome notes (rebooked, paused, not interested)
Home-visit planner with route order, check-in and check-out by location, and visit confirmation from the patient side
Therapist session log feeding a monthly pay statement for per-session staff
Insurance and direct-billing tracker with document checklist per claim type, submission dates, rejections and payments
Co-pay and daily cash close reconciliation
Referral source tracker with monthly volumes per referring practice
Lead inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and Google enquiries with response timer
Equipment register and repair log; consumables reorder list
Owner dashboard: utilisation per therapist, sessions delivered, package completion rate, revenue by payer
Simple content calendar for social posts approved by the clinic

exchange.text: Most of our patients buy a 10-session package and vanish after 4 or 5. Then they come back months later asking for their remaining sessions.
So packages are being left half-used, and old balances come back to you later. Noted. When someone misses a couple of booked sessions, does anyone get in touch with them?
No, we only notice when they turn up again.
Got it, there’s no early signal when someone drops off. Noted. How do you keep track of how many sessions each person has left right now?
